newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were both expected to open steady to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

A weak boxed beef market should keep packer bids light and mostly at $64 per cwt, which would prompt carryover pressure in nearby live cattle futures. Bear spreading may continue, which would support deferred months, analysts said.

Bullish projections on Friday's semi-annual cattle inventory report and death losses from recent bitter cold weather and snowstorms in the northern Plains and upper Midwest should keep deferreds supported, they said.
Early projections on the inventory report put total U.S. cattle supplies as of January 1 mostly down one to three percent from last year.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to follow the lead of live cattle futures with a lower index also cited as a selling factor in nearbys. As in live cattle, deferred months were seen showing support following new contract highs Tuesday, analysts said.
Most early estimates on the inventory report for cattle under 500 lbs, feeders, points to a decline of one to three percent and a 1996 calf crop unchanged to two percent lower.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.22 at $69.55 per cwt.
